title: Testing in Spring: JUnit 5, Mockito, MockMvc, test slices and Testcontainers
seriesDescription: Micrometer and tracing, Spring Security and JWT, JUnit, Mockito and Testcontainers. JEE-Advanced style: integer, assertion-reason, matrix match, fill-in-the-blanks, short code and multi-correct questions.
description: JUnit 5 lifecycle and parameterised tests, Mockito stubbing and strictness, MockMvc, Spring Boot test slices and context caching, @DataJpaTest rollback and Testcontainers with @ServiceConnection.
source: JUnit 5 User Guide; Mockito documentation (MockitoExtension, strict stubs); Spring Boot reference (Testing: slices, MockMvc, @MockitoBean, Testcontainers); Spring Framework testing reference; Testcontainers for Java documentation

questions.prompt: Write a JUnit 5 test method for `PriceService` (it has a `PriceRepo repo` field) that stubs `repo.find("A")` to return 10, calls `svc.price("A")`, asserts the result is 10 and verifies that `repo.find("A")` was called once. Assume `repo` is a Mockito mock and `svc` is already built.
questions.explanation: Annotate the class with `@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)` and use `@Mock` / `@InjectMocks`. BDDMockito `given(...).willReturn(...)` and AssertJ assertThat are equally valid.

questions.prompt: Write a JUnit 5 test method `priceRejectsNull` that asserts `svc.price(null)` throws `IllegalArgumentException`, using `assertThrows`.

checks.label: uses assertThrows with the exception class

questions.explanation: `assertThrows` returns the exception, so you can assert on its message too. It replaces the JUnit 4 `@Test(expected = ...)` attribute, which has no equivalent in JUnit 5.

questions.prompt: Write a JUnit 5 parameterised test `add(int a, int b, int expected)` that runs for the rows (1, 2, 3) and (0, 0, 0) from inline CSV values and asserts `a + b` equals `expected`.
questions.explanation: Each row runs as its own test in the report. `@ValueSource` covers a single argument, `@MethodSource` supplies complex objects. The `junit-jupiter-params` module is needed.

questions.prompt: Write a `MockMvc` call that GETs `/api/orders/42`, expects HTTP 200 and expects the JSON field `id` to equal 42. Assume a `MockMvc` named `mockMvc`.
questions.explanation: `@WebMvcTest(OrderController.class)` with a `@MockBean`/`@MockitoBean` service gives a fast web-layer test. `perform` `throws Exception`, so the test method declares `throws Exception`.

questions.prompt: Match each Spring test annotation or library to what it provides.

right.text: Controller slice with `MockMvc` and no service beans
JPA slice with an embedded database and rollback after each test
A real database in Docker started for the test
A mock web server for outgoing HTTP

questions.explanation: Slices load only part of the context for speed. Use Testcontainers when H2 differs from production (`jsonb`, partial indexes, locking behaviour).

questions.prompt: In a Spring Boot 3.4+ test, which annotation replaces a bean in the application context with a Mockito mock?

options.why: This creates a mock outside the Spring context; the real bean stays wired.
It enables Mockito annotations in plain unit tests and leaves the Spring context alone.
It injects whatever the context holds, with no mocking.
Correct: it registers a Mockito mock in the Spring context (it supersedes `@MockBean`).

questions.explanation: `@MockBean` is the older, deprecated spelling. Each distinct set of mocked beans yields a different context key, which affects caching speed.

questions.prompt: Read the assertion A and the reason R, then choose the correct relationship between them.
questions.assertion: `@DataJpaTest` tests roll back their changes by default.
questions.reason: Each `@DataJpaTest` test runs inside a transaction that Spring rolls back when the test ends.

whys.a: Correct: The rollback of the test-managed transaction is exactly why the data disappears.
whys.b: Not this one: Both are true but R is not the reason A holds does not describe this pair; R is actually the reason or is false.
whys.c: Not this one: A is true while R is false does not describe this pair; check the truth of R again.
whys.d: Not this one: A is false while R is true does not describe this pair; check the truth of A again.

questions.explanation: Remember that rollback also hides flush-time constraint errors; call `flush()` or `entityManager.flush()` when you want them to surface.

questions.prompt: Read the assertion A and the reason R, then choose the correct relationship between them.
questions.assertion: Mocking collaborators makes a unit test fast and isolated.
questions.reason: Since Mockito 5 the inline mock maker is the default, so final classes can be mocked.

whys.a: Not this one: Both A and R are true and R explains A does not describe this pair; R does not explain A.
whys.b: Correct: Both are true, but being able to mock final classes is not what makes tests fast and isolated.
whys.c: Not this one: A is true while R is false does not describe this pair; check the truth of R again.
whys.d: Not this one: A is false while R is true does not describe this pair; check the truth of A again.

questions.explanation: Do not mock types you do not own or simple value objects; wrap them in an adapter you control instead.

questions.prompt: Read the assertion A and the reason R, then choose the correct relationship between them.
questions.reason: `@SpringBootTest` always opens a real HTTP server on port 8080.

whys.a: Not this one: Both A and R are true and R explains A does not describe this pair; R does not explain A.
whys.b: Not this one: Both are true but R is not the reason A holds does not describe this pair; R is actually the reason or is false.
whys.c: Correct: A is true. R is false: the default web environment is a mock servlet environment with no listening port.
whys.d: Not this one: A is false while R is true does not describe this pair; check the truth of A again.

questions.explanation: Use `webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT` with `TestRestTemplate` or `WebTestClient` when you need a real server.

questions.prompt: Read the assertion A and the reason R, then choose the correct relationship between them.
questions.assertion: To isolate a class in a unit test you should mock the class under test itself.
questions.reason: Mocks replace collaborators with controllable stand-ins.

whys.a: Not this one: Both A and R are true and R explains A does not describe this pair; R does not explain A.
whys.b: Not this one: Both are true but R is not the reason A holds does not describe this pair; R is actually the reason or is false.
whys.c: Not this one: A is true while R is false does not describe this pair; check the truth of R again.
whys.d: Correct: A is false: mocking the class under test means you are no longer testing it. R is true, but it concerns collaborators.

questions.explanation: Mock the dependencies of the class under test. Use a spy only when you must partially stub a real object.

questions.prompt: Read the assertion A and the reason R, then choose the correct relationship between them.
questions.assertion: With `@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)`, a test that stubs a method it never calls fails.
questions.reason: `MockitoExtension` uses strict stubs by default, so an unused stubbing is reported as `UnnecessaryStubbingException`.

whys.a: Correct: Strict stubs turn dead stubbings into failures.
whys.b: Not this one: Both are true but R is not the reason A holds does not describe this pair; R is actually the reason or is false.
whys.c: Not this one: A is true while R is false does not describe this pair; check the truth of R again.
whys.d: Not this one: A is false while R is true does not describe this pair; check the truth of A again.

questions.explanation: Remove the dead stub, or mark a shared setup stub with `lenient().when(...)` or `@MockitoSettings(strictness = LENIENT)`. Strictness catches stale tests.

questions.prompt: True or false: using different `@MockBean` (or `@MockitoBean`) sets in different test classes can force Spring to build additional application contexts.

options.why: Correct: the mock set is part of the context cache key.
Contexts are cached by configuration, and each distinct mock set is a different configuration.

questions.explanation: To keep builds fast, share a base test configuration and avoid scattering `@MockBean` over many classes.

questions.prompt: True or false: with `@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT)` and a test-level `@Transactional`, data written by requests sent through a real HTTP client is rolled back when the test ends.

options.why: The server handles the request on its own thread, outside the test-managed transaction.
Correct: the rollback only covers work done on the test thread.

questions.explanation: Clean up explicitly (delete by id, truncate in `@AfterEach`) or use `MockMvc`, which runs on the test thread.

questions.prompt: Complete the Testcontainers setup for Spring Boot 3.1 or later.
questions.text: Put {1} on the test class so containers are started and stopped, mark a static PostgreSQLContainer field with {2}, and add {3} to it so Spring Boot wires the datasource without a @DynamicPropertySource method.
questions.explanation: A static container is shared by all tests in the class (faster); a non-static one restarts per test. `@ServiceConnection` needs the `spring-boot-testcontainers` dependency. Without Boot 3.1, `@DynamicPropertySource` with the container's `getJdbcUrl()` is the classic route.

questions.prompt: A JUnit 5 test class has 3 `@Test` methods and uses the default lifecycle. How many instances of the test class does JUnit create to run it?
questions.explanation: The default is `Lifecycle.PER_METHOD`, a new instance for every test method, which isolates field state. `@TestInstance(PER_CLASS)` would create just 1 and allow non-static `@BeforeAll`.

questions.prompt: A class has 2 plain `@Test` methods, one `@RepeatedTest(3)` method and one `@ParameterizedTest` with a `@CsvSource` of 4 rows. How many test executions does JUnit report?
questions.explanation: 2 + 3 + 4 = 9. Repeated and parameterised tests report each repetition or row as its own invocation under the parent method.

questions.prompt: Create a `java.time.Clock` named `clock` fixed at the instant `2024-02-29T00:00:00Z` in UTC, so a test can control the current time.
questions.explanation: Inject the Clock into the class under test and call `LocalDate.now(clock)` or `Instant.now(clock)` instead of the no-argument versions. The production bean is `Clock.systemUTC()`.
